messages.content: Explain how a bicycle stays upright.

Mostly through steering. When the bike leans, you (or the bike itself) steer slightly into the lean, which moves the wheels back under the centre of mass. Speed helps because the gyroscopic effect of the wheels and the geometry of the front fork give self-correcting steering.
explain it to a 6 year old

When you start to fall to one side, you turn the handlebars a tiny bit that way, and the wheels catch up under you. That's why you can't stand a bike up when it isn't moving, but when you ride, it keeps catching itself.
What is DNA?

DNA is the molecule that stores genetic instructions in living things. It's a long double-helix chain made of four bases (A, T, C, G), and the order of the bases encodes the instructions for building proteins.
go deeper on how it gets copied

During replication, the double helix is unwound by helicase and each strand serves as a template. DNA polymerase adds matching bases (A with T, C with G) to build a new strand, working in one direction on the leading strand and in short fragments on the lagging strand, which are joined by ligase. Proofreading by the polymerase keeps errors very low, about one in a billion bases after repair.
what is gravity
Gravity is the attraction between objects with mass. The more massive something is, the stronger its pull. It keeps us on the ground and the Moon in orbit around Earth.
now the einstein version

In general relativity, gravity isn't a pull but the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Objects follow the straightest possible paths in this curved spacetime, which look like orbits or falling. It predicts effects such as light bending around massive objects and time running slower near strong gravity.
How do I run a meeting that doesn't waste everybody's time?

Share an agenda in advance with a purpose and desired outcome, invite only people who are needed, start and end on time, assign a note-taker and write down actions with owners and dates. If it can be an email, make it one.
my manager micromanages me

Try to understand what drives it: usually anxiety about outcomes. Proactively give short updates before they ask, agree on what 'done' looks like at the start, and ask for autonomy on specific tasks as trust builds. If it continues, a direct but friendly talk about how you work best can help.
How do I write a good out-of-office message?

Say when you're away and when you'll return, who to contact for urgent things, and whether you'll check email. Example: "I'm away until 12 May with limited email access. For urgent matters, please contact Sam at sam@example.com. I'll reply when I return."
Should I accept a counter-offer from my current employer?

Be cautious. Ask why they're offering more now and not before, and whether the underlying reasons you wanted to leave (growth, culture, manager) would change. Money alone often doesn't fix those. If your reasons were purely pay and the offer addresses them with a clear path forward, it can make sense.
What should I put in a thank-you email after an interview?

Send it within 24 hours. Thank them, mention one specific thing from the conversation that interested you, reaffirm why you're a good fit in a sentence, and say you're looking forward to next steps. Keep it under 120 words.
how to deal with imposter syndrome

Keep a record of your wins and positive feedback, and read it when doubt hits. Remember that most people feel like they're figuring it out as they go. Talk to a mentor or peer, since they usually share the feeling. Treat the feeling as a thought, not as evidence.
is it ok to cry at work

Yes, it's human and happens to many people. If you need a moment, step away to a quiet place, wash your face and breathe. If it's happening often, that's useful information about stress or the workplace, and talking to someone you trust or a counsellor can help.
Write a polite follow-up email: I applied two weeks ago and heard nothing

Subject: Following up on my application for [Role]

Hello [Name],

I applied for the [Role] position on [date] and wanted to check on the status of my application. I remain very interested in the role and would be glad to provide any further information.

Thank you for your time,
[Your name]
How do I take better notes in lectures?

Don't transcribe; listen for ideas and write in your own words. Leave space, mark questions, and review and tidy the notes within 24 hours. Cornell-style layout (notes, cues, summary) works for many students.
I understand the lecture but fail the exam. Why?

Understanding while someone explains differs from recalling and applying on your own. Practise with past papers and self-testing, explain concepts aloud without notes, and work problems before looking at solutions. That's the kind of effort the exam will demand.
What's the Feynman technique?

Pick a concept, explain it in simple language as if to a child, notice where you stumble or use jargon, go back to the source to fill those gaps, then simplify again. It shows what you don't really understand.
Is it better to study in the morning or at night?

Whichever fits your alertness and schedule. Evidence suggests that sleep after learning helps consolidation, so heavy cramming late at night is less effective than studying earlier and sleeping. Use your sharpest period for the hardest material.
how do I choose a college major

Look at what you enjoy and do well in, then check what careers each major leads to and what the typical courses are. Talk to students and graduates, take introductory classes in two or three fields, and remember that many careers don't map one-to-one to a major.
Can I study with music on?

Instrumental or ambient music can help some people, especially with repetitive tasks. Music with lyrics usually hurts reading and writing. If you notice yourself listening instead of working, switch to silence or white noise.
How much water should I drink?

A common guide is around 2 to 3 litres of total fluid a day from drinks and food, but needs vary with weather, activity and body size. Pale yellow urine is a simple sign you're doing fine. Thirst is a reasonable guide for most healthy people.
does cold weather cause colds?

Not directly. Colds are caused by viruses. In winter people spend more time indoors close together, which makes spread easier, and some viruses survive better in cold dry air. Being chilled isn't the cause in itself.
What's a healthy breakfast?

Something with protein, fibre and some healthy fat to keep you full: oats with fruit and nuts, eggs with wholegrain toast, or yoghurt with berries and seeds. Heavily sweetened cereals and pastries tend to leave you hungry sooner.
How do I start meditating?

Sit comfortably for five minutes, focus on your breath, and when your mind wanders, which it will, gently bring attention back. That return is the exercise. Apps and guided recordings can help you start.
is it bad to crack your back
Occasional back cracking is usually harmless. If it's painful, repeated forcefully, or comes with numbness or weakness, see a clinician. Don't try forceful self-manipulation of the neck.
how can I get better at waking up without coffee

Fix the basics first: consistent bedtime, seven or more hours of sleep, morning daylight and some movement. Drink water on waking. Taper caffeine gradually rather than stopping suddenly, to avoid headaches.
Why do I get a headache when I skip meals?
Low blood sugar, dehydration and caffeine withdrawal are common causes. Regular meals and enough water often help. If headaches are severe, frequent, or come with vision changes, see a doctor.
how do I speed up my slow computer?

Restart it, close heavy programs, and check Task Manager for what's using CPU or memory. Uninstall unused apps and disable startup programs. Make sure there's free disk space, run updates and a malware scan. If it's an old hard drive, upgrading to an SSD makes the biggest difference.
What's the difference between 4G and 5G?

5G offers higher peak speeds, lower latency and can support more devices at once than 4G. Real-world speeds depend on the network, your phone and signal; in many places 5G is only modestly faster than good 4G.
should I update my phone to the latest OS right away?
Security updates are worth installing promptly. Major version upgrades are safer after a week or two, once early bugs are reported. Back up your phone first either way.
How do I back up my photos?

Use the 3-2-1 idea: three copies, on two different kinds of storage, with one off-site. For example, your phone, an external drive at home, and a cloud service. Check now and then that the backups actually open.
why does my laptop get so hot

Common causes are blocked vents, dust in the fan, heavy background processes, or using it on a soft surface. Use it on a hard surface, clean the vents with compressed air, and check what's using the CPU. If the fan is always loud even when idle, it may need servicing.
What is two-factor authentication?

It requires a second proof of identity in addition to your password, such as a code from an authenticator app or a hardware key. Even if someone steals your password, they can't log in without it. Apps or hardware keys are safer than SMS codes.
Is incognito mode private?
Only partly. It doesn't save your history or cookies on that device after you close the window, but websites, your employer or school, and your internet provider can still see your activity.
what is an emergency fund

Money set aside for unexpected costs such as job loss, medical bills or urgent repairs. A common target is three to six months of essential expenses, kept somewhere safe and easy to reach like a savings account.
How do credit scores work?

A credit score estimates how reliably you repay debt, based on factors like payment history, how much of your available credit you use, length of credit history, new applications and mix of accounts. Paying on time and keeping balances low are the biggest levers. Scoring models differ between countries.
Is it smart to buy things on a payment plan?

It depends on the terms. Interest-free plans can be fine if you reliably pay on time and the item is something you need. Plans with high interest or late fees cost more, and they can encourage spending you wouldn't do with cash.
what is diversification
Spreading your money across different investments so that one poor performer does less damage. The saying is not to put all your eggs in one basket. Index funds are a simple way to diversify.
Should I invest or pay off student loans?

Compare rates: if your loan interest is higher than what you can reasonably expect from investing, pay it down. For low-interest loans, you might split between the two. If your employer matches retirement contributions, take the match first, as it's an instant return.
how can I make rice less sticky

Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear to remove surface starch, use a measured ratio (about 1 cup rice to 1.5 cups water for long-grain), and don't stir while it cooks. Let it rest covered for 10 minutes and fluff with a fork.
How do I keep guacamole from turning brown?
Brown colour comes from oxidation. Add lime juice, press plastic wrap directly on the surface so there's no air contact, or cover with a thin layer of water and pour it off before serving.
can I freeze cooked pasta
Yes. Cook it slightly under, toss with a little oil, cool it, and freeze in portions for up to 2 or 3 months. Reheat in boiling water or in a sauce. Texture is slightly softer than fresh.
what's a good substitute for buttermilk
For each cup, stir 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar into a cup of milk and let it stand for 5 minutes. Plain yoghurt thinned with a little milk also works.
how long does cooked chicken last in the fridge
About 3 to 4 days in a sealed container at 4 C or below. Reheat until steaming hot. If it smells off or looks slimy, throw it out.
Why is my bread so dense?

Frequent causes are too little kneading or rising time, old yeast, too much flour, or cold dough. Try proving until the dough has roughly doubled, check that your yeast foams in warm water first, and weigh the flour rather than scooping.
How do I improve my English writing?
Read widely, write a little every day, and read your work aloud. Keep sentences short, prefer active verbs and cut filler. Ask someone to give you feedback and notice patterns in the corrections.
What's the difference between 'who' and 'whom'?

Use 'who' for the subject ("Who called?") and 'whom' for the object ("To whom did you speak?"). A trick: if you can answer with 'he', use who; if 'him', use whom. In casual speech, 'who' is often used for both.
Can you proofread: 'Their going to the park tomorow, weather or not it rains.'
Corrected: "They're going to the park tomorrow, whether or not it rains." Fixes: 'Their' to 'They're', 'tomorow' to 'tomorrow', and 'weather' to 'whether'.
what does 'cache' mean and how do I say it
A cache is a place that stores copies of data so it can be fetched quickly later. It's pronounced like 'cash'.
what is the plural of 'octopus'?
Both 'octopuses' and 'octopi' are used, but 'octopuses' is the most widely accepted. 'Octopodes' is the Greek-derived form, rarely used.
How do I learn kanji

Learn them in small sets, starting with the most frequent and those with simple components, and study them in words, not in isolation. Use spaced repetition (such as Anki), practise writing a few each day and read simple texts for reinforcement.
Why did World War I start?

The trigger was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in June 1914, but deeper causes included alliances, militarism, imperial rivalries and nationalism. Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, and the alliance system pulled in Russia, Germany, France and Britain.
Who was Cleopatra?

Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, reigning from 51 BCE to 30 BCE. She was Greek-Macedonian by descent, spoke many languages and allied with Julius Caesar and then Mark Antony. After their defeat by Octavian, she died by suicide, and Egypt became a Roman province.
what was the cold war in simple terms

A long rivalry, from about 1947 to 1991, between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies. They never fought each other directly, but competed through arms races, spying, space exploration and support for opposing sides in other countries' wars.
Was Vlad the Impaler the real Dracula?

He was an inspiration for the name. Vlad III of Wallachia was known for impaling enemies and was called 'Dracula', 'son of the dragon'. Bram Stoker borrowed the name for his 1897 novel, but the vampire story itself is fiction.
what caused the 2008 financial crisis

A mix of risky mortgage lending, the bundling of subprime mortgages into complex securities, banks with too little capital, and weak oversight. When house prices fell, borrowers defaulted, the securities lost value, and major institutions like Lehman Brothers failed, which froze credit worldwide.
what is the difference between weight and mass
Mass is how much matter an object contains and doesn't change with location. Weight is the force of gravity on that mass, so it changes: you weigh less on the Moon but your mass is the same.
how do vaccines work

A vaccine shows your immune system a harmless piece or version of a germ, so it learns to recognise it. If you later meet the real germ, your body responds faster and more strongly, often preventing serious illness.
What is photosynthesis?

The process plants, algae and some bacteria use to turn light energy into chemical energy. Using sunlight, they convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and release oxygen: 6 CO2 + 6 H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2.
why is the moon sometimes visible in the day

The Moon orbits Earth and is above the horizon for part of the day as well as the night. It's bright enough to be seen against the daytime sky when it's well away from the Sun, such as in the first and last quarter phases.
what causes earthquakes
Earth's crust is divided into tectonic plates that slowly move. Stress builds up where plates grind, stick and then suddenly slip along faults, releasing energy as seismic waves.
What is entropy?

A measure of disorder, or more precisely the number of microscopic arrangements consistent with a system's state. The second law of thermodynamics says that the entropy of an isolated system tends to increase, which is why heat flows from hot to cold, and why you can't unscramble an egg.
what's the difference between a hurricane and a typhoon

They're the same type of storm, a tropical cyclone, named differently by region: hurricane in the Atlantic and northeast Pacific, typhoon in the northwest Pacific, and cyclone in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific.
Respond only with yes or no: is Paris in France?
Yes.
answer in exactly five words: why exercise?
It keeps your body healthy.
no emoji and no fluff: tell me how to boil pasta
Boil salted water. Add pasta. Cook for the package time, tasting a minute early. Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water if you'll make a sauce.
Can you be more enthusiastic?
Absolutely! I'm happy to bring more energy. What are we working on today?
talk to me like a calm coach
Okay. Take a breath. Tell me what's in front of you, and we'll take it one step at a time. What's the first thing you need to move forward?
Use bullet points: reasons to learn a second language

- Better job opportunities in many fields
- Easier travel and deeper connection with other cultures
- Cognitive benefits such as improved attention and flexibility
- Delays in age-related decline for some people
- Access to books, films and music in the original language
Explain what a mutual fund is in the style of a sports commentator

And the mutual fund steps up to the field. Hundreds of investors pool their money, a manager picks the stocks, and everyone owns a slice of the whole team. Look at that diversification! Fees might trip it up, so keep an eye on the cost.
What's the tallest mountain on Earth?

Mount Everest is the highest above sea level, at about 8,849 m. Measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller, and measured from the Earth's centre, Chimborazo in Ecuador is the farthest point.
how tall is Mauna Kea
About 4,207 m above sea level. Counting from its base on the ocean floor, it's over 10,000 m tall.
How many time zones does Russia have?
Eleven.
and the US?
Six in total, if you include Alaska and Hawaii: Eastern, Central, Mountain, Pacific, Alaska and Hawaii-Aleutian. With the territories it's more.
What's the longest river in the world?
It's debated between the Nile (around 6,650 km) and the Amazon (around 6,400 km, with some measurements suggesting it's longer). The Nile is traditionally listed as longest.
why is it debated?

Because rivers are hard to measure: it depends where you define the source and the mouth and how you account for the twisting channels. Different surveys of the Amazon's source give different lengths.
Who invented the telephone?
Alexander Graham Bell is credited with the first practical telephone patent in 1876. Others, like Elisha Gray and Antonio Meucci, worked on similar ideas.
was it stolen?

That's disputed. Gray filed a related caveat the same day, and Bell's patent was later challenged in court. Meucci's earlier work was recognised by the US House of Representatives in 2002. Most historians say several inventors were close, and Bell won the legal race.
what's the deepest part of the ocean
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, about 10,900 m (nearly 11 km) deep.
has anyone been there
Yes. Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh descended in 1960, and film director James Cameron went solo in 2012. More recent descents by submersibles like Victor Vescovo's have followed.
Who painted the Mona Lisa?
Leonardo da Vinci, painted in the early 16th century.
where is it now
It hangs in the Louvre Museum in Paris, behind protective glass.
What's the smallest country by area?
Vatican City, at about 0.44 square kilometres.
and by population?
Also the Vatican City, with roughly 800 residents. Several tiny countries, like Tuvalu and Nauru, are larger but still have small populations.
How old is the Earth's oldest tree?
Some bristlecone pines in California are about 4,800 years old. A clonal Norway spruce in Sweden, known as Old Tjikko, has roots about 9,500 years old, but the trunk above ground is much younger.
so which counts?

It depends on your definition. For a single continuously living stem, the bristlecone pine holds the record. If you count a clonal organism with old roots, Old Tjikko or even the Pando aspen clone can claim much more.
